suggestions.comment: Consider a deterministic regression that moves the integration branch after identity validation but before Git merge, demonstrating that the immutable persisted commit, rather than the moved branch, is merged. The implementation already passes integration.head directly; this would protect that important property against future regressions.

Consider adding merge-conflict and overlapping dirty-checkout cases to assert propagation of Git's nonzero status and preservation of the user's existing work. The current implementation delegates these checks to Git and propagates its status correctly.

summary: Independent review of the complete four-file tracked diff, untracked shell integration tests, CLI callers, and original findings found no blocking shell/CLI defects. Merge requires persisted acceptance, canonical repository identity, matching Git common directories, and the recorded integration branch/HEAD; it merges the immutable recorded commit. Acceptance validates integration identity, tandem is opt-in, Git coloring uses global configuration, and share --once reports remote/push failure while continuous sharing retries. Focused execution passed all 24 tests across both files (20 integration and 4 shell tests); both CLI scripts passed Node syntax checks and git diff --check passed. The separately addressed share credential-filter findings were outside this review. Only the requested review JSON was written; no source edits, live providers, heavy suites, commits, pushes, or merges of the reviewed repository were performed.
